post.description:
Ranks every cluster of the environment for a namespace of this tier, and holds the first that still fits for 15 minutes
(placement.yaml `reservation`): 201 with its `placementId`. The create then sends `placementId`, which turns the hold into the request's own
(docs/02, "Placement"). `dryRun=true` ranks and holds nothing: the portal's preview.

Each cluster is either ranked, best first, or excluded with a named reason: not connected, not writable, placement disabled,
outside the region, zones or clusterSelector, stale or partial snapshot data, no size, maxNamespaces reached, no CPU or
memory headroom after committed quota and active reservations, and in prod no headroom after losing its largest zone. CPU
and memory are checked separately. Nothing calls Thanos: the facts are the stored snapshots, the watch of each cluster and
the active holds.

Ranking needs capacity:read in the environment; the hold needs namespaces:create there too. A team holds at most 3 active
placements in an environment: a fourth is 429 rate-limited until one is claimed or lapses. When no cluster can be held,
422 `no-placement` lists every exclusion. plugins.yaml can stop placement in an environment: 422 `plugin-disabled`, the dry
run too, after the permission check.

**Requires** `capacity:read`.

Opens a delete request: the folder leaves Git after approval, every file of it at any depth, and the namespace waits
in awaiting_prune until an operator confirms the prune. Needs If-Match, read as on a change: a list of tags passes when one
of them is the current etag, and `*` is 428 `precondition-required`. A folder that holds a submodule is 409
`folder-holds-submodule`: its removal would change `.gitmodules`, outside the folder.

`dryRun=true` answers 200 with the plan and opens no request: `changes` lists every file of the namespace's folder, at
any depth and whatever made it, as `removed`, `files` is empty, and `approval` is the approval that the delete would need
now. It makes the delete's planning checks, so they refuse it where they refuse the delete: the permission, If-Match, a
protected namespace (422 `namespace-protected`) and a submodule (409 `folder-holds-submodule`). Like every dry run it skips the Idempotency-Key and the namespace's lock: while
another request holds the namespace the plan is still 200, and the delete is 409 `change-pending`.

patch.description:
Changes a namespace that exists: its tier, its custom quota and limits, and its labels and annotations.

**Merge patch.** `labels` and `annotations` follow JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7396):
a key that the body leaves out keeps its value, a string sets it, and `null` removes it. `x-cmapi-edit` of each key,
in `GET /api/v1/metadata-keys` and, for the keys that file does not declare, in `git.edits` of the namespace's read,
says how it may change: `fixed` (the value in Git stays; the same value sent back is accepted; a missing key that
starts the name can be added with that start), `automatic` (filled at creation; a change keeps Git's value, and a request
can add a missing one with the derived value), `required` (it changes and is never removed) or `optional`. A key that no
rule admits can be removed, never set. A `sensitive` key adds one approval to the request.

**Check, then submit.** With `dryRun=true` the answer is 200 with the plan, and no request is opened. `metadataDiff`
lists each effective change by key as `before`, `after` and `source`: `before` is `null` when the key is added, `after`
is `null` when it is removed. The same body without `dryRun`, with an Idempotency-Key, opens the request (202).

**If-Match.** Send the ETag of `GET .../namespaces/{ns}` as If-Match (RFC 9110, section 13.1.1). For a new plan,
a namespace missing from Git is 404 `object-not-found` before the precondition checks. For an existing namespace,
missing If-Match is 428 `precondition-required` (RFC 6585, section 3), and so is `*`: it proves no read, so cmapi
refuses it on purpose, where RFC 9110 lets it match any namespace that exists. A list of tags, sent in one If-Match
field, passes when one of them is the current etag, by the strong comparison, so a weak tag (`W/"..."`) never matches.
Otherwise the answer is 412 `precondition-failed` (RFC 9110, section 15.5.13) with the current `etag`: read the
namespace again, apply the change to it and send it.
An Idempotency-Key replay still requires If-Match, but does not compare it again: it returns the
original request in its current state even after Git moves, and `*` is 428 there too. The Idempotency-Key parameter
says when a retry is a replay. A non-dry-run submission also requires Idempotency-Key (400 without it).
One request at a time holds a namespace: while another is open, 409 `change-pending` names it in `requestId`.

**Refusals.** 422 `policy-violation` has one `errors` entry for each key that breaks a rule (`reserved_key`,
`invalid_key`, `invalid_value`, `derived_key`, `missing_required_key`, `too_many_keys`, `annotations_too_large`).
A key that only an operator may change is 403 `forbidden` without `namespaces:protect` in the namespace's
environment. A body that changes nothing is 422 `no-change`.

**Several ResourceQuotas.** cmapi changes only its own ResourceQuota (`<ns>-quota`) and LimitRanges (`<ns>-limits-*`);
every other one in the folder is kept as Git holds it, each in its own file (#250). When the folder holds several
ResourceQuotas, a change of `quota` or `tier` is 409 `several-resource-quotas`, which names them in `resourceQuotas`: the
request cannot say which one it changes. When none of them is `<ns>-quota`, a change of `limitRange` is refused too, and
a change of labels, annotations or the expiry keeps every ResourceQuota and LimitRange.

**Requires** `namespaces:write`.

as they are: only what the API server sets is dropped, and each key under a skip prefix of adoption.yaml only when that
changes nothing on the cluster. It adds its own system keys and the tier `custom`; each ResourceQuota and LimitRange keeps
its name, in its own file. Each difference from the instance's rules is a finding of the plan, never a change: a wrong or
missing key, a value beyond the custom bounds, a policy failure that the namespace already holds (`policy-ratcheted`).

The request needs one approver of approver-platform, and one more when the plan has findings; no automatic approval covers
it. After approval the bot opens the pull request. cmapi reads the objects again before it pushes the branch and in the pull
request's check: a change since the plan fails the request (`adoption-plan-stale`), and the label removed cancels it.

`dryRun=true` answers 200 with the plan, its files, findings and approval, and opens no request.

answer is the instance's, the same for every caller; it has a strong ETag. If-None-Match answers 304, and an If-Match
that does not list the ETag answers 412.
